sense: sketch out the main points of a story or essay

terms.gloss: run briefly over the main points
terms.grammar: adverb with percurrō; also summātim perscrībere, write out in brief
evidence: Varr. RR 2 pr. 7: breviter ac summātim percurram (Lewis & Short s.v. summātim)
Cic. Att. 5.16.1: aliquid summātim perscrībere (Lewis & Short)
Plin. NH 35.89: imāginem in pariete carbōne (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 34: outline the story, dēlīneā (dēlīneāte) fābulam (tractātum)
terms.comment: In Lewis & Short only of sketching a picture; we have found no classical instance of it for outlining a story or an essay, as Traupman uses it.
Lewis & Short: late Latin (Tertullian) for fōrma, dēscrīptiō.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency.
Lewis & Short: summatim · Lewis & Short: delineatio
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
